h1: Make AI Food and Drink Videos From a Bottle Photo
lead: Static bottle and can photos can't show the pour, the fizz or the glass a shopper imagines drinking from. Turn one package photo into a vertical food and drink video with ice, bubbles and a fresh pour, built for TikTok and Reels.
intro: A quick, close-up pour is the whole idea: your drink flowing from bottle to glass. The sample shows sparkling orange juice splashing over ice next to a sliced orange, with whole fruit on a cutting board behind it.

A short pour puts the drink's color, fizz, and texture in motion. Use it for juices, sodas, cold brew, kombucha, sauces, or syrups. A 6-second clip can show one pour, while 10 seconds leaves room for a slower pour and a final look at the full glass.
tip: Upload a photo with the bottle upright and the liquid color visible, then mention the glassware, the ice, and what sits on the counter.

faq.q: What source photo works for a drink clip?
faq.a: Use a straight-on bottle or can photo with the full package and liquid color visible.

faq.q: Can the video show a pour?
faq.a: Describe one pour into a glass and keep the package in view during the action.

faq.q: Where can I add flavor names?
faq.a: Type flavor names, prices, and serving notes in your editor after download.

faq.q: Can the clip show ice and condensation?
faq.a: Yes. Describe the glass, ice, and pour in the scene and the generated clip keeps your can as the product.

faq.q: What length fits a pour clip?
faq.a: Six seconds covers one pour; 10 or 15 seconds fit a pour plus a tasting beat; 30 seconds gives room for prep, pour and first sip. Video jobs cost 24, 40 or 60 credits for 6, 10 or 15 seconds, shown before you run them.

faq.q: Should the can label be blank?
faq.a: Use a clean product photo without a date sticker; add brand or flavor text as a separate layer when needed.

faq.q: Can I use a street taste test for a drink ad?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the creator chest-up, show one small sip, and hold the bottle or can beside the glass so the serving context is clear.

faq.q: What should a kitchen tutorial show?
faq.a: Show one preparation step, such as pouring oat milk into iced coffee, with the package, receiving glass, and liquid color visible.

faq.q: How do I make an ASMR can-opening clip?
faq.a: Ask for a close hand shot of the pull tab, condensation, and first fizz, then add licensed sound or keep the recorded click after download.

faq.q: Where do flavor and allergen details go?
faq.a: Add the exact flavor, ingredient, and allergen wording as editable text after download from your approved package information.

faq.q: How do I choose 6 seconds versus 10 to 15 seconds?
faq.a: Choose 6 seconds for one pour, sip or opening click; choose 10 or 15 seconds when the clip needs preparation plus a final glass or tasting beat, and 30 seconds for a longer serving story.

faq.q: Can I use these videos as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Clips you make can be used in your own paid campaigns on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and other channels, and downloads carry no AIVideosUGC watermark.

faq.q: Do I need a studio or a creator for a pour shot?
faq.a: No. The pour, ice and garnish are generated from your package photo, so you skip the studio, the props and shipping samples to a creator.

overview.h2: Make the liquid do the explaining
overview.d: A strong pour scene has three anchors: the package, the receiving food or glass, and one visible texture change. Ask for the liquid to flow, fizz, foam, or glaze while keeping the label and product color in view.

overview.h2: Use the short version for the first sensation
overview.d: Six seconds can capture an opening splash or a quick drizzle; ten, fifteen, or thirty gives the viewer more time to see ice settle, foam rise, or a full glass reach its final level. Keep one pour per clip so the action stays legible.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a package for a pour scene

items.d: A straight bottle, can, pouch, or jar photo gives the generated scene a stable shape to carry into the counter setup.
For translucent drinks or sauces, use a view where the liquid color is visible instead of hidden behind a dark label.
Name a tumbler, coupe, bowl, plate, or spoon so the pour has a clear destination and scale.
Say crushed ice, foam, fizz, syrup ribbon, or glaze; one texture cue gives the shot a specific job.

results.h2: What the finished pour can show

items.d: The package stays part of the composition while the liquid moves into a glass, bowl, or over food.
Choose 9:16 for TikTok or Reels, 1:1 for a product gallery, 16:9 for a wider placement, or 4:3 and 3:4 for another crop.
Six, ten, fifteen, and thirty seconds cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits; the charge is visible before you submit.

scene_recipes.h2: Pour scenes for food and drink products

items.d: A chilled bottle pours into a tall glass with orange peel, cubes, and a bright counter catching the bubbles.
